source: Reuters, Nov 5, 2026, as carried by CNA (its page is dated Nov 6, 2026)
text: Reuters reported, by two people it did not name, that “about 600,000 of Nvidia’s advanced artificial intelligence chips are stored in Hong Kong awaiting shipment to China”, “as Beijing withholds approval for large-scale imports despite demand from technology firms”. The report’s next sentence calls them “the stockpile of H200 chips”.

source: Financial Times, Nov 27, 2025, as carried by The Irish Times
text: The Financial Times, citing two people it did not name, reported that Alibaba and ByteDance “are among the tech groups training their latest large language models (LLMs) in data centres across Southeast Asia”, “to access Nvidia’s chips”. The report names no site. It says Chinese companies “typically sign a lease agreement” for data centres abroad, that clusters “have boomed in Singapore and Malaysia”, and that many are “equipped with high-end Nvidia products”.

The Financial Times reported that advanced Nvidia chips owned by Datasection, a Japanese firm, in a data centre “outside of Osaka” were “at the disposal of one customer: China’s Tencent”. The naming of Tencent rests on the paper’s unnamed people: Datasection’s chief executive “declined to confirm the Tencent deal”. Tencent said its use of “cloud computing services is both transparent and legal”. Datasection’s own notices, which do not name their customer, run as follows. Jul 10, 2025: a contract with the customer for an AI data centre to be opened in Osaka prefecture. Nov 7, 2025, a release: a site secured for an AI data centre in Inzai, Chiba, “新たな国内プロジェクトとして” (as a new domestic project). Jan 6, 2026: the start of that service at its first centre in Japan put back to March 2026; since September 2025 the customer had been served on a partner’s GPU servers, and the notice names neither the partner nor where its servers are. May 7, 2026: the first centre’s site changed from Osaka to Inzai, with no date given for the change (the next record). None of the four says where the customer was served in December 2025.

source: Datasection (listed in Tokyo), notice of May 7, 2026, in Japanese, as mirrored by irbank.net
text: Datasection’s own notice: on its customer’s request for shorter latency it changed the site of its first AI data centre in Japan from Osaka to Inzai, in Chiba (“その開設地を本件顧客（以下に定義します。）からのレイテンシー（データ送信から応答までの時間）の短縮要望を受け、大阪府から千葉県印西市に変更いたしました”: its site was changed from Osaka prefecture to Inzai, Chiba, on the customer’s request to shorten latency, the time from sending data to the response), and signed a contract to buy 635 servers with 5,080 Nvidia B300 chips for it, to start in stages from May to July 2026. The notice does not name the customer: it calls it one of the world’s largest cloud service providers. Later, by the firm’s own words: on Jul 17, 2026 it “has begun taking delivery of GPU servers equipped with NVIDIA’s latest B300 GPUs at its first AI data centre in Japan, which is currently being prepared for operation”; on Nov 16, 2026 it said that for one AI data-centre project in Japan and two abroad, expected to start in stages from July 2026, the expected start of full operation had slipped (“フル稼働の開始見込時期に遅れが生じておりました”); the filing does not name the sites.

source: Licence table of BIS (H200 licence and application status as of May 11, 2026), released by the House Foreign Affairs Committee, Nov 19, 2026
text: The licence table of May 11, 2026 from the US Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) lists five applications, with Nvidia as exporter, covering 1,118,500 chips, with these three countries listed as the intended destinations. The entries name data-centre operators or ultimate consignees associated with ByteDance, BytePlus, TikTok and Alibaba. All five applications are marked “RWA” (returned without action). The table gives no reasons. An application names a data-centre operator or ultimate consignee; it is not an order. The sum is mine.

According to Reuters, the Wuxi municipal government “said in March 2025 that a computing cluster using Nvidia H800 processors had entered operation”. The report names the province and the city government; it names no site.

source: Bloomberg, as summarised by Tom’s Hardware, Jul 11, 2025
text: Plans for 39 data centres, “mostly in Xinjiang and Qinghai”, name more than 115,000 Nvidia chips, by Bloomberg’s review of investment documents, tenders and filings. The summary adds that “there is no direct proof” the chips have been obtained.
A proposed 6.2 billion yuan computing centre “seeks commercial partners and specifies Nvidia H100 chips”, by Reuters’s review of projects.

By Reuters’s review, Sinomach, which Reuters calls a state-owned engineering group, said a subsidiary won a contract in a 3 billion yuan computing-centre project “specifying Nvidia H100 and H200 processors”.
A 2.26 billion yuan project that combines Nvidia H100 processors with Chinese-developed chips is described in “an April government prospectus”, by Reuters’s review.

A 1.5 billion yuan development “proposes installing 625 Nvidia H200 servers”. Chinese industry reporting in June “said construction had begun on two buildings in its first phase”, by Reuters’s review.

A computing centre here “plans to install approximately 3,072 Nvidia processors”, by tender documents that Reuters says specify H100 and H200 hardware. A 1.16 billion yuan building contract was awarded in July. “The documents do not establish whether the processors have been delivered.”
